items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: And there was some advantage to being an American musician who had not just listened to the records but been there and seen it. I mean Peter Frampton and Eric Clapton were both completely obsessed with playing the blues.

ctx.x: I wonder, I’m picturing a scenario that you write home to whomever and, “Yeah studies are going good and yeah, and I’m doing sessions with Eric Clapton and the Rolling Stones.”

I didn’t write that. It was such a smaller scene back then. Like if you say the Rolling Stones now what you picture is a billion dollar organization going around the world in © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

trucks and planes and stuff. But back, this was 1967, 1968 — I mean they were well known, they had some hit records, but there was a scene — this one particular recording studio, it was called Olympic Studios, it was outside of London. I went to school in Brighton, which was a one hour train ride up to London. And while I was in graduate school friends of mine from San Francisco had come over to England, they had been signed to Capitol Records and they were going to make their first record in England. And so I…
